instructions: Set an oven rack about 4 inches under the broiler and turn the broiler to high. Prick each eggplant a few times with a fork and put them on a foil-lined sheet pan.
Broil the eggplants for 15 to 18 minutes, turning them every 5 minutes, until the skins are blackened and the eggplants have collapsed. Cooking them over a gas flame works too.
Meanwhile, dice the onions fine. Mince the garlic. Chop 1 tbsp of the parsley.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Break it up and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, until it's browned.
Add the onions and cook for 4 minutes, until soft. Add 2 of the garlic cloves and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomato paste, red pepper paste, pul biber, black pepper and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Stir for 2 minutes, until the pastes darken.
Add 1/3 cup water and simmer for 3 minutes, until the beef is juicy but not watery. Take the pan off the heat.
Let the eggplants cool for 3 minutes, then peel off the skins and chop the flesh fine. Transfer it to a sieve and press out the liquid for 2 minutes.
Mix the eggplant with the yogurt, the last garlic clove and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Spread the eggplant mixture on a platter and spoon the beef and its juices on top. Sprinkle with the parsley.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Serve right away.
method_notes: No version with 20 or more ratings could be read, so Cooking Gorgeous (5 from 7 ratings) leads. It and Hungry Paprikas (5 from 3) agree on smoked eggplant folded into thick yogurt with garlic and salt, and a browned meat topping with tomato and red pepper paste. Ground beef stands in for the lamb, the broiler or a gas flame chars the eggplant, and the roasted vegetable garnish is left out to stay near 35 minutes. Aleppo pepper replaces chili flakes to keep it mild.
